doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers halls and the picnic boat
title: Joe Yetta's ballroom at the Cut-Off and Charlie McDonough
summary: Martin recalls the ballroom run by Joe Yetta at the Cut-Off, where Tom played, and says Charlie McDonough took over as manager afterward.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oh yeah. I was following it. Yeah. I was on the levee. Run down the levee. Run down the levee, follow it from Cunhal Street down there. You could hear it all the way. All the way down. Follow that. Wish I could have heard that. Now you take, after that you take, had a fella down there they called Joe Yetta. Joe? Joe Yetta. He run the ballroom, they had a hole down there at the Cut-Off. Yeah. When I, he used to play down there.

Yeah, I played down there. That's right. Played down there. And then. What year that was in? Oh, that's, that's around 1907, the eight. Back up in there. Yeah. Because Charlie McDonough, he was, he come there after Julietta. Yeah. Charlie McDonough, the colored fella. They all played there for Charlie McDonough. Yeah, I played for all of them. He was the manager then, the Dungle of the Spikes. That's right, Charlie McDonough.
